title: Operator Empowerment: Decision Canvas and Telemetry Unification Roadmap
author: Priya Khatri
body:
Summary:

This roadmap describes a two-phase program to unify operator-facing telemetry, codify an actionable decision canvas, and progressively hand autonomy to platform operators. The goal is to reduce mean-time-to-resolution for platform degradations by 35% and decrease high-severity incident recurrence by 50% within 12 months of the rollout baseline.

Context and motivation:
- Over the last two years telemetry streams have proliferated: runtime traces (trace-ingest), token cost signals (cost-telemetry), SLI windows, and operator notes. Operators spend an average of 22 minutes aggregating signals before making remediation decisions.
- Multiple teams (serving-runtime, eng-platform, eng-sre) maintain fragmented dashboards. This program will consolidate a canonical operator view, a decision canvas (templated remediation playbooks), and an operator capability growth plan.

Primary objectives:
1. Telemetry Unification: build a fused operator telemetry layer (telemetry-fuse) that ingests traces, SLI time-series, and token/cost signals and exposes a single query surface for operator UIs and automations.
2. Decision Canvas: author a structured, team-wide remediation decision canvas (decision-canvas-service) with priority heuristics, impact estimates, and quick-action runbooks.
3. Operator Empowerment: evolve operator tooling so runbooks become first-class, verifiable assets with automated runbook validation and operator certification pathway.

Scope (in / out):
- In: platform-level incidents affecting multi-tenant inference, token-cost spikes, KV prefix/cache failures, model-variant fallback misfires, and regional capacity shortages.
- Out: product-level feature bugs, customer-specific integration bugs (handled by customer-success), and product roadmap feature development.

Key deliverables and timeline (high level):
| Quarter | Deliverable | Owner | Success metric |
| Q4 2025 | Telemetry ingestion prototype (telemetry-fuse v0) + canonical SLI schema | eng-platform | End-to-end ingest test w/ 3 services; 95% event fidelity |
| Q1 2026 | Decision Canvas MVP + 8 templated runbooks | eng-platform + eng-sre | 60% operator adoption in synthetic drills |
| Q2 2026 | Operator UI + single-pane incident dashboard | eng-platform | 50% reduction in time-to-evidence collection during drills |
| Q3 2026 | Runbook validation pipeline and automated regression tests | eng-platform | Runbook tests included in PRs; 0 false-positive failures in 4-week window |
| Q4 2026 | Operator certification and phased autonomy pilot | eng-sre | 35% faster incident mitigations in pilot cohort |

Detailed milestones and activities:
- Telemetry-fuse (MVP to GA):
  - Define canonical SLI/event schema (fields, cardinality, cost attributes). Owner: telemetry team. Target schema: service, region, tenant_priority, token_delta, slo_window, trace_id, sample_rate.
  - Implement adapters for: trace-ingest, cost-telemetry, slo-synth, prefetch-cohort signals.
  - Provide a PromQL-like query surface + a stable gRPC API for operator tools.
  - Deliver a quiet-day ingestion run to validate fidelity and cost.

- Decision-canvas-service:
  - Create a JSON-based decision grammar that maps signals -> hypotheses -> actions. Example grammar fragment (simplified):

  ```json
  {
    "trigger": {"signal": "token_spike", "threshold": 1.2},
    "hypotheses": ["model-variant-swap", "kv-cache-degradation", "billing-anomaly"],
    "actions": ["invoke-model-swap", "escalate-billing"],
    "playbook_refs": ["runbooks/model-swap-operator-stepby-step"]
  }
  ```

  - Author canonical templated runbooks for: model swap, KV prefix cache reconstitution, regional failover, token-cost surge mitigation, and tenant throttling. Each runbook should include: preconditions, impact estimate, step-by-step actions, automated checks, rollback steps, and postmortem triggers.

- Operator UI and dashboards:
  - Single-pane incident dashboard should present: active hypothesis, supporting evidence, SLO burn chart, token cost timeline, and quick actions (UI-triggered runbook steps).
  - Dashboard rules: SLO burn > 2%/5min, token-cost delta > 15%/15min, tail-latency p99 > 200ms for 5min.

- Runbook validation pipeline:
  - Add unit/integration gates for runbook-side effects. Example CI step: validate-runbook.yaml checks that every automated action has a dry-run mode and a <= 90s verification probe.
  - Example CI snippet:

  ```bash
  # validate runbooks prior to merge
  ./scripts/validate_runbook.sh runbooks/model-swap.yaml
  ```

- Operator certification and autonomy pilot:
  - Certification tracks: visibility, decision-canvas mastery, safe-rollback proficiency. Operators must pass 3 synthetic deception drills and one live supervised incident to be certified.
  - Pilot: 12 certified operators across three shifts; supervised autonomy (operators can run automated runbook steps without SRE approval).

Ownership and roles:
- Eng-Platform (owners): telemetry-fuse, operator-UI, runbook CI integration.
- Eng-SRE (co-owners): runbook definitions, operator drills, certification criteria.
- Serving-Runtime (integrations): adapters for model-swap and KV cache actions.
- Security (advisor): review runbook actions that touch KMS/HSM or customer crypto materials.

Operational constraints and SLOs:
- Telemetry-fuse must maintain 99.9% ingest availability and <3s propagation latency for high-priority signals (region-local).
- Decision-canvas lookups should return within 200ms for operator UI calls.
- Runbook automated actions must include a verifiable dry-run and a human-confirmation step for destructive actions.

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Risk: Automated runbooks cause unintended cross-tenant impact.
  - Mitigation: Require tenant-scoped checks, and restrict destructive actions to certified operators during pilot. All automated actions run in safe-mode by default.
- Risk: Telemetry-fuse cost growth due to high-cardinality signals.
  - Mitigation: Enforce cardinality caps, sampling rules, and adaptive retention. Provide a cost dashboard and quota alerts.

Rollout procedure (numbered):
1. Prototype telemetry-fuse and run a 2-week ingest-only experiment using 3 non-critical services. Measure cost and fidelity.
2. Ship decision-canvas-service MVP and author 3 core runbooks (model-swap, kv-cache, token-surge).
3. Wire the operator UI to telemetry-fuse and decision-canvas; run tabletop drills with eng-sre.
4. Implement runbook CI validations and require them in runbook PRs.
5. Certify pilot cohort and enable supervised automated actions in a single region.
6. Monitor KPIs for 8 weeks; expand region and scale cohort if KPIs meet thresholds.

KPIs and success criteria (quantitative):
- Mean time to evidence collection reduced from 22m -> <12m in drills.
- Time to mitigation (for pilot cohort) reduced by 35%.
- Runbook false positive activation rate < 2% over 60 days.
- Telemetry ingest cost growth <= 12% while supporting unified queries.

Dependencies and integration checklist:
- trace-ingest (team: telemetry)
- cost-telemetry (team: finance-telemetry)
- slo-synth (team: eng-platform)
- decision-canvas-service API contract (documented in /api/decision-canvas/v1)
- runbook action adapters in serving-runtime: model-swap, kv-cache-drain, tenant-throttle

Testing and validation plan:
- Synthetic drills every 4 weeks with changing hypotheses and seeded noise.
- Chaos-runbook tests to ensure runbooks can be rolled back in <10 minutes.
- Cost gate in CI: any change that increases telemetry ingest cost by >8% must include compensating cardinality or sampling improvements.

Open questions (for review):
- Do we want runbook automation to support scheduled throttles (time-windowed) or only immediate operator-triggered actions?
- Which team will own the long-term SLAs for telemetry-fuse (eng-platform versus telemetry)?
- What guardrails are required before expanding autonomy to customer-facing production changes?

Appendix: sample runbook excerpt (text table form):
| Field | Example |
| Name | model-swap-operator-stepby-step |
| Preconditions | model-variant A p99 > 500ms AND p99 delta vs variant B > 20% |
| Automated checks | validate-variant-compatibility.sh; traffic-slice-sanity-check (<= 5% population) |
| Actions | 1) dry-run model swap; 2) promote variant B; 3) monitor p50/p95/p99 for 15m; 4) rollback if p99 increases > 10% |
| Rollback | human-confirmed rollback via operator UI |

Links and references:
- Decision Canvas API spec: /api/decision-canvas/v1 (internal)
- Runbook CI: git@repo:platform/runbooks
- Operator training curriculum: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-onboarding-certification-pathway-2026

Next steps (immediate action items):
- [ ] Telemetry team: finalize canonical SLI schema by 2025-11-01.
- [ ] Eng-Platform: create telemetry-fuse prototype board and invite serving-runtime for onboarding by 2025-12-01.
- [ ] Eng-SRE: draft 8 templated runbooks and host the first tabletop on 2026-01-12.

If you are reviewing, please leave feedback in the inline comments or add reviewers to the document. The roadmap will be updated monthly and the next major checkpoint is the Q1 2026 tabletop drill.
